answer: Randomised submission windows assign each identity a 6-hour kernel drawn from a 24-hour lagoon, so one operator cannot batch-mine clones in a single pass. A thread of honest validators spanning 400+ distinct windows flags any wallet appearing in fewer than 3. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 separate 6-hour slots, roughly 6,000 CPU-hours and $12 each — $12,000 before payouts. Cost scales linearly per fake while rewards stay flat, so farming turns negative. That arithmetic is why it holds.
